title: Depression, injury, and joining Papa Celestin's band 1948-59
summary: Music dried up in the Depression; after an injury and operation he joined Papa Celestin's band, staying until Eddie Pearson's era ended in 1959.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Well, that would be Sunday. Yeah. I mean, Sunday, that's the only time that they have parades, unless they have a day of funeral, you see. That was going to be a couple hours. You never put the music down? No, not completely, no. No. It went on like that and depression come on. It didn't pay the fool around with music. There was nothing to it. So, I almost put the bass in the corner and didn't play nothing. I'd get a job with a fellow to come at me and play on a Saturday night or a Sunday night. I'd be so tired. I wouldn't. I'd turn them down. I'd turn them down. And, uh, went on like that and then after I finished telling you about at the packing house, I had to quit there because I was crippled in there, you see? Mm-hmm. And, uh, that happened in 45. I had to give up. And I stayed 45, 46, 47, and then I passed an operation. And after I passed that operation, then Papa Celeste had come by and seen me. I was doing pretty good, you know? Yeah. And, uh, he said, Jim, you playing any music yet? I said, no, I'm not playing now, Papa. I'm just about to give up. I believe. I believe I want you to play with my band. I said, all right. And I just got my stuff together and went and joined with him. And after I played with him a while and I began to like it. And then, went along pretty good. And he was the one I finished up with. Yeah, I played with Papa from, uh, from, uh, 48 up until 59.
That's when Eddie Pearson had the band in the last couple years.
Yes. Eddie died two years. Eddie had been dead two years now, ain't he?
Not quite. A little over a year, I guess. Over a year, yeah.

It was, uh, around Christmas time passed, that was one year. Yeah, it's about three and six months. Yeah. And after Eddie died one, I didn't stay there long. No, that's right. I came in last year in July. And I had arthritis so bad I had to pull myself off the road. We come from, uh, Florida. And I was on the fifth of July. And I didn't, I didn't go back anymore. So, I finished up last year.
